This is a very commonly misinterpreted piece of data. What you're referring to is the idea that there is more genetic variation within each race than there is between races. This is undeniably true. The misinterpretation of this data is when people use it to conclude that there is no difference between the races. The average variation doesn't change the fact that some genes are more prevalent in some races and not others, and that these genes can cause some races to have certain characteristics that are rare or absent in others.

Let me give an analogy that ELI5s this whole thing. Let's say Chinese people range in height from 4'6 and 6'0", with an average of 5'3". Further, let's say Africans range in height from 5'0" to 7'0", with an average of 6'0". The variation between the races (difference in average) is 9", while the variation within the Chinese people is 18" and the Africans is 24". So you could say that there is more height variation within each race than there is between the races. However, you couldn't then make any claims about both races being equally tall.

De Mille asked her whether she knew who had first spoken that line. "It doesn't make any difference who spoke it," persisted the woman. "It means that God would forsake someone, and it has to come out."

"My dear lady," intervened the clergyman at this point, "I wonder whether you are aware that those words were said by Jesus on the cross."

De Mille won his point.
